The moon is up and the pond is still. Rest your tail now.
Even the reeds are nodding off. Time you did too.
My boat is moored and the heron is gone. Go bunk down.
A slow day ends like a slow tide. Sleep in it, friend.
The lanterns are dimming all over Nekomura. Yours can too.
No fish bites in the dark. No cat should either.
The crickets have taken over the night. Let them sing you down.
My whiskers feel the dew coming. Curl up before it lands.
A calm pond means a calm morning. Sleep toward it.
The stars are counting themselves tonight. You count sheep.
The old pier is ready for silence. So is your pillow.
Night is just the pond pulling its blanket up. Heh.
The heron has tucked his beak. You tuck your paws.
Morning will need you fresh as a new net. Off to bed.
The mist is creeping low over the water. Go above it.
Fish dream of deep currents. You dream of dry blankets.
The village is quiet as a held breath. Let yours out slow.
A tired cat makes a tangled cast. Sleep it off.
My lamp is out and my tale is told. Yours ends here.
The tide has slipped past the dock. Let the day slip too.
Even the minnows have gone to their stones. Follow suit.
The wind has lain down for the night. You lie down too.
A good day knots itself off at dusk. Yours is knotted.
The pond keeps its fish till dawn. You keep your rest.
Old bones and young bones both need the dark. Go on.
The moon is a patient fisherman. Let it watch alone.
No heron to chase and no line to mend. Bedtime, friend.
The water is black and kind tonight. So is sleep.
Nekomura is yawning behind its shutters. Yawn with it.
A still night makes a strong morning. Take the trade.
The gulls have all gone to their ledges. You go to yours.
My pipe is cold and my boots are off. Yours next.
The reeds are whispering slow lullabies. Hear them out.
One more dawn will come whether you wait or sleep. Sleep.
The tide does not hurry and neither should you. Off now.
Even the oldest proverb ends in quiet. Heh. Here is yours.
The pond is a dark mirror with no fish in it. Look, then rest.
A cat who rests reels in a better morning. Believe that.
The night mist is soft on tired eyes. Close yours soon.
My boat sleeps on its rope and I sleep on my cot. Join me.
The last cricket is winding down. Let it finish for you.
No tide turns without a pause. Pause here, friend.
The village dogs have all hushed. Take the hint kindly.
A calm harbor asks for a calm keeper. You have kept it.
The stars will mind the pond till light. You mind your bed.
Even the heron respects the dark. Show him you can too.
My nets are folded and my worries are few. Fold yours too.
The night is long and the fish are patient. You be patient.
The water has gone to sleep already. Catch up with it.
A fisherman's best catch is a full night's rest. Heh.
The moon has climbed the mast of the sky. Let it sail.
Sleep is bait for a strong morning cast. Take the hook.
The pond has closed its shutters of mist. Go inside too.
No fish worth losing sleep swims tonight. None at all.
The reeds are still and the pier is still. You be still.
Old whiskers twitch at dreams of fat carp. Dream on, friend.
The tide clock says low and late. So does this old cat.
The darkness is a warm blanket over Nekomura. Pull it up.
Even the moonfish has gone below. Go below your quilt.
My tale is done and the fire is low. Yours should dim.
